I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is what I know best, the machines fit it, the buyers are easy to find, and the risk is lower than trying something fancy at my age. I am 73, so I will not spread myself across too many crops or do management that is too complicated. I will grow winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I will use improved seed rather than old saved seed, because I want steadier yield and better disease resistance, but I still want something familiar and easy to manage. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive amounts, because input costs matter and too much fertilizer does not pay well. Water is always important in Hebei, so I will irrigate wheat more carefully and maize only when needed. I will plough before wheat to prepare the field well, then use rotary tillage after wheat harvest to quickly plant maize. For pests and disease, I will spray only as much as needed to protect the crop and avoid wasting money.
